what: Codex jury (codex exec, read-only, neutral prompt) on the built Evidence Article, Awwwards weights: Design 40, Usability 30, Creativity 20, Content 10. Inputs: phone 390x844 and desktop 1440x900 captures of every section (qa/article-capture.mjs), as four contact sheets.

rounds.verdict: A cohesive, emotionally engaging result page with standout world-building, but repetitive presentation and a demanding mobile reading experience keep this screenshot-based assessment below Site of the Day level.
strengths: The pearl-marble islands, oval mirrors, glass Genii and lavender palette establish a recognizable visual world with strong continuity.
Expressive serif headlines bring editorial character to a game interface; the upright and italic archetype names distinguish the two readings elegantly.
The dark surprise spread provides a convincing change in mood and one of the strongest image–copy compositions.
Specific lines such as 'Yours show up a week later' feel observant and intimate without sounding clinical.
Desktop compositions adapt meaningfully across sections instead of simply enlarging the phone layout.
Rooms, paired archetypes and Genii's prediction record make the result feel like a personal game artifact.
weaknesses: The mobile navigation exposes only part of seven destinations at once; repeated tiny icons add little differentiation, and later sections are difficult to discover.
Supporting labels, stat explanations and record captions are visually subordinate to the point of becoming difficult to scan, especially against pale backgrounds.
The long sequence repeats similar affirmations across the lede, traits, rooms and two sides; reading effort grows faster than insight.
Repeated island illustrations and rounded pastel cards reduce the distinctiveness of individual traits and sections.
The stat system combines unfamiliar axis names, endpoint names, dots, intensity words and badges without an immediately obvious reading order.
Party compatibility sounds more certain than the visible explanation supports; 'your opposite' is especially reductive.
Screenshots cannot establish interaction quality, keyboard access, motion behavior, loading performance or actual touch-target sizes.
top_fixes: Redesign the phone section navigation around a clearly labeled current section and an accessible section menu; keep direct jumps available without requiring discovery through horizontal scrolling.

Increase small supporting text and its contrast, especially in stat expansions, trait provenance, room descriptions and prediction captions; check the page at actual phone size rather than only in presentation sheets.
Simplify each stat row to axis, selected endpoint and one clearly explained strength indicator; reveal secondary badges and opposite-end detail only inside the expansion.
Edit repeated personality claims so every section contributes a distinct example, tension or consequence; shorten the lede and remove trait copy that merely restates the stat label.
Give the mobile trait carousel an explicit position indicator and clear next-card affordance, and make the whole card a labeled flip control rather than relying on the small corner button.
Strengthen the rooms interaction by visibly connecting the selected map pin to its corresponding text and placing the selected description directly beneath the map on mobile.

Explain the basis of party matches in one concrete sentence per match and frame them as playful possibilities; finish with one dominant action and a clearer bridge from quiz insight to the game's daily experience.

sections.name: cover
sections.note: The strongest expression of the brand: compelling fantasy scenery and confident archetype typography. On phone, the large landscape-to-title sequence pushes the promise and summary chips toward the fold.

sections.name: lede
sections.note: Warm, legible editorial framing with effective desktop columns. Both passages lean heavily toward affirmation, and the life summary needs a more concrete observation to distinguish it.

sections.name: stats
sections.note: Expandable rows provide useful depth, but the competing layers of terminology make a simple six-axis profile feel complicated. The expanded interpretation is more intelligible than the indicators above it.

sections.name: traits
sections.note: Attractive desktop grid and consistent card craft. Repeated mirrors and islands communicate the world more effectively than the individual traits; mobile hides much of the collection behind a horizontal interaction.

sections.name: surprise
sections.note: Excellent tonal contrast, atmosphere and typographic emphasis. The observation lands emotionally, although 'the thing you didn't know' promises more novelty than another flattering assertion necessarily delivers.

sections.name: rooms
sections.note: The island map turns life contexts into a memorable spatial metaphor. Desktop pairs map and explanation well; phone separates them enough to weaken the relationship between selecting and reading.

sections.name: two sides
sections.note: The two Geniis at one table make the dual-archetype premise charming and understandable. The conflict paragraph adds valuable tension, but the trait-name formulas require recall of earlier terminology.

sections.name: open book
sections.note: The most incisive writing, especially the delayed-feelings observation, paired with an inviting private-room image. The reassurance that it is 'more charming than you think' softens the honesty before the reader can feel it.

sections.name: record
sections.note: A distinctive way to give Genii personality and make the quiz feel reciprocal. The large score is effective, but repeated glowing capsules and muted misses do too little to explain individual outcomes.

sections.name: party
sections.note: Clear social intent and useful contrast among the slots. Stacked archetype names are awkward to scan, and compatibility claims need more persuasive reasoning than a changed stat or a blanket opposition.

sections.name: closing
sections.note: Beautiful return to the opening world, with a readable conversion card. The copy introduces the game premise late, while the invitation to test friends competes with the download as the natural next step.

rounds.note: after the round 1 fixes: phone section menu with reading progress, calmer stat rows, larger captions, card dots and whole-card flip, rooms selection under the map, party hierarchy, record marks, copy edits
rounds.verdict: An unusually cohesive, emotionally articulate result page, but repetitive art direction, uneven reading density and under-explained interactions keep it below my Site of the Day threshold.
strengths: The pearl-marble islands, oval mirrors and glass Genii establish a recognizable world that carries consistently across both breakpoints.
Expressive serif headlines give the results editorial authority; the italic second archetype makes the dual identity immediately legible.
The dark surprise spread creates a strong cinematic interruption, giving one personal observation more impact than another card would.
The copy often translates personality labels into recognizable behavior: shared calendars, the spare key and feelings arriving a week later.
The desktop two-sides composition makes the relationship between the archetypes visually understandable, with Genii figures between complementary and conflicting behaviors.
Mobile layouts show deliberate adaptation, particularly the stacked party cards and compact section navigation.
weaknesses: Usability is assessed from screenshots; actual tap targets, animation, keyboard access, screen-reader behavior and interaction feedback remain unverified.
Small supporting text, pale labels and faint boundaries weaken readability, particularly in navigation, provenance lines and the record cards.
Repeated islands, mirrors, rounded cards and lavender gradients gradually lose their expressive purpose; distinct psychological ideas receive similar visual treatment.
Desktop pacing alternates between substantial empty space and dense card collections, while mobile accumulates a long sequence of similarly weighted sections.
The mobile traits carousel conceals most of the collection, and visible flip controls appear inconsistent across cards without a clear explanation.
The rooms map has several intricate landmarks but little obvious differentiation in function; the accompanying list communicates more efficiently than the map.
The page mixes stat names, endpoints, traits, archetypes and relationship labels faster than it explains their relationships.
Some intimacy feels asserted rather than earned, especially presenting authored lines as 'In your own words' and declaring who the player clicks with.
top_fixes: Increase the size and contrast of supporting copy, section navigation and stat annotations at actual device size; make every interactive label comfortably readable without zooming.
Give each trait card an explicit, consistent flip affordance and add a visible mobile position indicator such as '1 of 6'; ensure the reverse includes an equally clear return control.
Tighten the vertical rhythm: reduce large transitional gaps on desktop and shorten repeated introductions on mobile so each scroll reveals a meaningful new idea.

Explain the six-stat system once in plain language, including what the five dots measure and how 'Clear', 'Strong' and 'Off the charts' relate to them; distinguish strength of preference from confidence in the result.
Make the rooms map and list visibly operate as one control: synchronize selection, emphasize the selected island and label decorative or unavailable islands appropriately.
Replace 'In your own words' with an honest framing such as 'Your result, in two lines' unless these are actual player quotes; connect the strongest personal claims to specific quiz choices.
Give the record section a clearer evidence hierarchy: show what Genii predicted, what the player chose and the outcome, with the explanation beside the '6 of 8' score.
Differentiate later sections with fewer repeated decorative assets and stronger compositional changes; finish with one concise transition into an app CTA that explains what the player can do next.

sections.name: cover
sections.note: The strongest branding moment: oversized editorial type, a clear dual identity and an inviting world. On mobile, the illustration postpones the actual result; the trait chips and reading-time detail feel much less resolved than the headline.

sections.name: lede
sections.note: The two summaries establish the social and personal dimensions with warmth and specificity. Desktop columns work well, but the declarations are uniformly flattering and the surrounding space could be tighter.

sections.name: stats
sections.note: Expandable opposites make the result inspectable rather than merely decorative. However, six vocabulary systems plus dots, intensity labels and a signature badge create unnecessary decoding work.

sections.name: traits
sections.note: Attractive collectibles with useful behavioral descriptions, but the repeated card structure and weak distinction between illustrative assets flatten the ideas. Mobile discovery and flip affordances need clarification.

sections.name: surprise
sections.note: The best individual spread: dramatic tonal contrast, restrained copy and a well-integrated character. The personal claim is compelling but familiar enough that its impact depends on evidence elsewhere.

sections.name: rooms
sections.note: An appealing attempt to make personality spatial. The map is visually busy relative to its information, and the selected state is clearer in the list than on the islands.

sections.name: two sides
sections.note: A valuable synthesis that explains both cooperation and friction between results. Desktop staging is excellent; the mobile stack separates the two observations and makes comparison harder.

sections.name: open book
sections.note: The delayed-feelings and hidden-recognition observations deliver the sharpest writing. The large decorative interior slows the mobile arrival, and 'In your own words' misrepresents authored copy unless it quotes the player.

sections.name: record
sections.note: Potentially the most distinctive mechanic, but currently presented as a dense results log. Tiny labels and an under-explained headline score obscure what Genii actually demonstrated.

sections.name: party
sections.note: A clear social continuation with useful visual differentiation between self, match and opposite. Compatibility sounds more definitive than the explanations justify, and the invitation could describe the friend experience more concretely.

sections.name: closing
sections.note: The return to the opening world creates a satisfying visual bookend. The transition into MirrorMii is emotionally consistent, but repeats familiar imagery and leaves 'your real day powers the game' more evocative than explanatory.

after_round_2.note: Fixes applied after round 2 (not re-judged; the brief allows one re-judge): a plain-language key for the beads, signature and wild card; every trait card turns over (stat cards show the other end) with a Turn back control and a card one of six indicator; Your side of it replaces In your own words; a caption for the faded islands and a larger selected islet; record explanation beside the score, status chips, single-column panes on phone; supporting text 14 to 16 px; tighter section rhythm.

checks.axe: qa/article-axe.mjs PASS (0 violations, phone and desktop, both voices, drawers open, card turned, menu open)
